question: What is the primary goal of palliative care?

options.A: Improving quality of life for patients and families
options.B: Speeding up the natural dying process
options.C: Providing care only during the final 24 hours

explanation: Palliative care centers on enhancing comfort and quality of life rather than chasing a cure for terminal conditions. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h1)

question: When should palliative care ideally be introduced to a patient?

options.A: When the family asks to stop all medications
options.B: Only after all curative treatments have failed
options.C: Immediately after the patient stops breathing
options.D: Early in the course of a serious illness

explanation: Early integration allows for better symptom control and psychological adjustment alongside active medical treatments. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h1)

question: How does palliative care view the dying process?

options.A: As a medical failure to be avoided at all costs
options.B: As a psychological condition requiring heavy sedation
options.C: As a normal part of the human life cycle
options.D: As an emergency that requires aggressive resuscitation

explanation: Palliative philosophy accepts dying as a natural progression rather than treating death as an enemy to be fought with futile interventions. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h2)

question: A patient-centered care plan in palliative nursing is primarily built around what factor?

options.A: Standard hospital routines for terminal wards
options.B: The financial budget of the healthcare facility
options.C: The personal values and goals of the patient
options.D: The personal preferences of the attending physician

explanation: True patient-centered care ensures that nursing interventions respect what the individual patient finds meaningful and important. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h2)

question: What are the four components that make up the total pain concept?
explanation: Total pain encompasses all these interconnected dimensions to explain why severe suffering occurs even when tissue damage seems minimal. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h3)

question: A patient with terminal cancer has maximal doses of opioids but still cries in pain and expresses fear of death. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Assess for psychological and spiritual sources of suffering
options.B: Restrict family visits to reduce social stimulation
options.C: Double the opioid dose immediately to induce sleep
options.D: Tell the patient that physical pain is now fully managed

explanation: Because pain is multidimensional, unrelieved distress often stems from non-physical components that require counseling or spiritual support. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of advance care planning in palliative care?

options.A: To state future treatment preferences before losing capacity
options.B: To guarantee that a patient lives for at least one more year
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital admissions
options.D: To transfer all legal liability away from the nursing staff

explanation: Advance directives allow competent individuals to outline their medical choices ahead of time for when they can no longer speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is active listening particularly critical during end-of-life conversations?

options.A: It shortens the duration of the clinical handover report
options.B: It uncovers hidden fears and unexpressed patient goals
options.C: It replaces the need for pharmacological symptom relief
options.D: It prevents the patient from asking difficult medical questions

explanation: Active listening helps nurses understand emotional needs and values that guide effective, individualized care plans. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which symptom is commonly managed using both opioids and positioning?
explanation: Low-dose opioids reduce the sensation of breathlessness, while upright or side-lying positions help maximize chest expansion. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is a key difference between curative care and palliative symptom management?

options.A: Palliative management prioritizes comfort even if cure is impossible
options.B: Palliative care avoids all prescription medications completely
options.C: Symptom management is only performed by medical doctors
options.D: Curative treatment focuses entirely on reducing physical pain

explanation: When disease eradication fails, the clinical goal shifts decisively toward maximizing comfort and quality of life. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h5)

question: What nursing intervention involves helping a patient reflect on their life history and achievements?
explanation: Life review allows patients to find meaning, reconcile past conflicts, and validate their personal legacy. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is addressing spiritual needs a vital part of palliative nursing?

options.A: Spiritual interventions replace the need for pain medications
options.B: It prevents family members from arguing over hospital bills
options.C: Spiritual distress can manifest as physical pain and anxiety
options.D: It is legally required to convert patients before discharge

explanation: Unresolved spiritual conflict contributes heavily to total pain, making spiritual support essential for holistic comfort. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h6)

question: Who is considered the 'unit of care' in palliative nursing practice?

options.A: The entire community surrounding the clinic
options.C: The patient and their family together
options.D: The attending physician and the nursing team

explanation: Palliative care recognizes that family members are deeply affected by the illness and require active assessment and support. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h7)

question: A grieving family member shows signs of prolonged, complicated grief months after a patient's death. What is the appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Advise them to take strong sedative drugs immediately
options.B: Tell them that time heals all wounds automatically
options.C: Refer the individual to professional counseling services
options.D: Encourage them to stop talking about the deceased person

explanation: Complicated grief exceeds normal mourning patterns and benefits from specialized mental health intervention. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which professional group forms the continuous, 24-hour hub of the palliative care team?
explanation: Nurses maintain round-the-clock contact with patients, coordinating care among all other team disciplines. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h8)

question: What is the primary benefit of using an interdisciplinary team approach?

options.A: Comprehensive care addressing multiple dimensions of suffering
options.B: Eliminating the need for any documentation or nursing notes
options.C: Reducing the hospital stay to less than twenty-four hours
options.D: Ensuring that the doctor makes all decisions without input

explanation: Different specialists collaborate to cover physical, social, emotional, and spiritual needs more thoroughly than any single clinician could. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h8)

question: What legal document allows a designated person to make medical decisions if the patient becomes incapacitated?
explanation: A medical power of attorney designates a healthcare proxy to speak on the patient's behalf when they can no longer communicate. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h9)

question: Why is withdrawing life-sustaining treatment ethically and legally distinct from active euthanasia?

options.A: Withdrawing allows the underlying disease to take its natural course
options.B: Euthanasia is legally permitted in all standard hospitals globally
options.C: Withdrawing requires a lethal injection administered by a nurse
options.D: Withdrawing treatment is only done without family consent

explanation: Stopping futile interventions removes artificial prolongation of dying, whereas active euthanasia involves an intentional act to cause death. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h9)
